channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: 24th National Fine Art Show · Peninsula Art League
item.description: The Peninsula Art League's annual juried show, now in its 24th year, returns to the Gig Harbor Vintage Aero Museum — a hangar of restored vintage aircraft that the League has turned into an exhibition venue. Photography and digital art are judged alongside two- and three-dimensional work, and the two jurors come from Pacific Northwest museums: Jessica Wilks, Director of Curatorial and Interpretation at Tacoma Art Museum, who has led curatorial teams for more than twenty years and shapes TAM's commitment to artists of the region; and Greg Robinson, Chief Curator at the Bainbridge Island Museum of Art, formerly director of the Museum of Northwest Art and a Betty Bowen Award committee member. More than $8,500 in cash prizes will be awarded. Open to artists 18 and over anywhere in the country; work must be original, made in the last two years, and not produced in a class or workshop. AI tools may be used in a supporting role for editing or minor enhancement but may not generate the artwork. Nudes, religious symbols, political themes and extreme violence will not be considered. All work must be for sale with a 15% commission; 2D pieces need D-rings and taut wire, no sawtooth hangers. Shipped work is accepted, at a $20 handling fee per piece. Jurying finishes 27 October and everyone is notified by 29 October. The show runs 14 November – 2 December 2026. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $55 first entry ($45 members) + $10 each addl. Prize: $8,500 in cash awards + Group exhibition.

item.title: 2nd Annual Kit Gilbert Juried Showcase · Ross Lynn Charitable Foundation
item.description: An open, themeless juried showcase at the Gilbert Center in downtown Ruston, Louisiana — a legacy project of the Ross Lynn Charitable Foundation that carries forward the work of two local artists, Ross Lynn and Kit Gilbert, the Ruston painter this annual show is named for. There is no set subject: any original work made since 2020 is welcome, and photography is explicitly among the media considered alongside painting, sculpture, mixed media, textile, ceramics and short video. The juror is Julie Crews, an oil painter based in Huntsville, Alabama who keeps an open studio and gallery at the 122-year-old Lowe Mill Arts and Entertainment complex and paints the domestic scenes of her own life — backyard fires, children swimming, errands around town. Two cash awards: the Juror's Choice / Best-in-Show at $750, and a People's Choice at $500 voted by visitors on opening night. Open to US artists 18 and over, up to three works, each needing a 250-word artist statement. AI-generated work is not accepted. Photographs must be framed or mounted — unframed works on paper and unmounted prints will be rejected — and artists arrange their own delivery and return shipping. Notifications 19 October, work due 7 November, exhibition 16 November 2026 – 15 January 2027 with a reception on 19 November. The Gilbert Center takes 30% commission. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: $12 per artwork. Prize: $750 Best in Show + $500 People's Choice.

item.title: Artifacts · 6 Bridges Gallery
item.description: A juried exhibition at 6 Bridges Gallery, a fine art and craft gallery on Main Street in Maynard, Massachusetts, built around the marks, remnants and meaningful objects that shape how we understand the world. The gallery is looking for work that uncovers the traces of what remains — hidden histories, personal relics, the quiet evidence of lives lived — and asks artists to think about what we carry forward, whether physical, emotional, cultural or imagined. All media are welcome except video and AI-generated work. The juror is Claudia Fiks, an independent curator and arts administrator of more than twenty years who founded and directs TAG | The Art Gallery at the New England Art Center in Boston's SoWa Art & Design District, directs Newton Open Studios, and writes on contemporary art for Artscope Magazine; she says she values authenticity, risk-taking, and work that communicates beyond the surface, regardless of medium or career stage. Open to artists 16 and over, up to three works made in the last three years, wired and ready to hang (no sawtooth hangers) and no larger than 40 inches in any direction. Three awards are given: the Artifact Award, Jurors' Choice and People's Choice. All work must be for sale and artists keep 60%. Work must be hand-delivered — the gallery does not accept shipped artwork. Notifications 9 September, drop-off 30 September – 3 October, exhibition 7 October – 14 November 2026 with a reception on 17 October. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $35 first entry + $5 each addl. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 26th Annual Juried Fine Art Show & Sale · Rockwall Art League
item.description: A three-day juried show and sale run by the Rockwall Art League in North Texas, open to artists across a five-state region — Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana and New Mexico — and now in its 26th year. Photography is one of eight judged categories, alongside oil, watercolour, acrylic, mixed media, mosaic, drawing and sculpture, and up to $6,600 in cash prizes is awarded across them — $1,000 for Best in Show, $500 and $200 for first and second in each category, plus a run of ribbon-only special awards. The two judges are Dana Brock, an abstract and mixed-media painter and Signature Member of the Southwestern Watercolor Society, and Rachel Townsend Cerny, founder of RTown Gallery in historic downtown Grapevine, Texas. The League says it exists to give both established and emerging artists a platform, and the event puts work in front of collectors and business representatives from across the DFW metroplex. Open to artists 18 and over; work must be original and made after 1 January 2024, and compositions based on published material, other artists' work, or generated with AI are not eligible. Work made in a class or workshop is out, as is anything containing nudes, conspicuously religious content, drug references or blatant political statements. Up to two works per artist, submitted with two to five images. New for 2026: hand delivery only — shipped work is not accepted — 2D pieces capped at 36 x 36 inches including frame, sculpture under 50 lbs, and a new venue at The Center at Rockwall City Place. Notifications go out 26 September; take-in is the morning of 16 October and the show runs 16–18 October 2026, with awards announced at the 16 October reception and final awards on the 18th. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $45 for up to 2 entries ($35 members) + $5 each addl. Prize: Up to $6,600 in cash prizes.

item.title: Summertime: Long Days, Lazy Days, Gentle Breezes · Arizona Photography Alliance
item.description: The second Juried Theme Gallery call of 2026 from the Arizona Photography Alliance, a Scottsdale-based non-profit now in its third year of online juried exhibitions. The brief is deliberately broad — summer as long days, lazy days and gentle breezes — and work in any medium is welcome, analogue, digital or alternative process, though AI-generated photography is not accepted. Independent juror Claire A. Warden, an interdisciplinary artist working in still and moving image whose cameraless abstraction has appeared in Harper's Magazine, Der Greif, Strange Fire Collective, Lenscratch and Light Work's Contact Sheet, selects one first-place winner for a $100 cash award plus two honourable mentions featured on AZPA's website and social channels. Every entrant is represented in the resulting virtual gallery — the juror picks one image from each submission — and all entrants may offer their chosen image for sale, handling any transaction directly. Open to members and non-members alike; joining brings the fee down to $25. AZPA board members may not enter. Submissions run August 1–16, 2026 through CaFÉ, with notifications on 30 August and the gallery going live on 1 September. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $25 members, $50 non-members. Prize: $100 + Online exhibition.

item.title: Seen/Unseen at Eric Fischl Gallery · Arizona Photography Alliance
item.description: A portfolio-based call from the Arizona Photography Alliance for a gallery exhibition at the Eric Fischl Gallery, perched atop Phoenix College's Fine Arts Building with panoramic views of central Phoenix. Seen/Unseen invites the full range of photographic methods and styles — from the tangible world we perceive to the hidden meanings and emotional states we sense — and asks for a cohesive body of work rather than single images. The juror is Emilia Mickevicius, Norton Family Assistant Curator of Photography in a curatorial post shared between Phoenix Art Museum and the Center for Creative Photography, previously curatorial assistant in SFMOMA's photography department, where she worked on Sightlines, Kinship: Photography and Connection and Sea Change. Selected applicants exhibit three to five works chosen from their submitted portfolio; all selected work is also presented as an online exhibition. Applicants must be current AZPA members at any level, though you need not live in Arizona — membership can be taken out at the time of applying. Accepted work must arrive exhibition-ready, shipped by 28 September or hand-delivered 29 September; the gallery retains 30% on sales. Exhibition runs 5–22 October 2026 with an opening reception on 5 October. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Fall Members Juried Exhibition · Wayne Art Center
item.description: Wayne Art Center's autumn members' show in the Davenport Gallery outside Philadelphia, juried both for entry and for awards. Eligible media run from painting and works on paper through ceramics, glass, fiber and jewellery to photography and 3D printing, so it is one of the few regional all-media shows where lens-based work sits alongside craft. Each member may submit exactly one original work made after 1 January 2024 and not previously shown at WAC — no second CaFÉ accounts, no exceptions. The juror is Peter Van Dyck, a Philadelphia painter who trained at the Florence Academy of Art and has taught at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, with solo shows at John Pence Gallery, Eleanor Ettinger Gallery and The Grenning Gallery. Open to Wayne Art Center 2026/2027 adult members aged 18 and over; membership can be taken out before applying. All accepted work must be hand-delivered to and collected from the centre — nothing shipped. Notifications 22 August, hand delivery 1 September, exhibition 8 September – 3 October 2026, with a reception and awards presentation on 20 September. — Deadline: August 5, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Celebrating Color · Edgewater Gallery
item.description: A national juried group exhibition at Edgewater Gallery, an artist-owned collective that has been part of downtown Fort Bragg on California's Mendocino Coast since 2003. The show takes colour in any form or dimension as its subject — atmosphere, emotion, memory, and the way chroma changes what we see — and the gallery says it is especially interested in work with a distinctive relationship to colour, whether through intensity, harmony, contrast, material presence or unexpected combinations. Photography is explicitly among the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, collage, fiber, sculpture and ceramics; AI-generated work, video and installation are not accepted. Open to artists 18 and over living in the United States, up to three works each, all of which must be original, for sale, and available for the full run. Two-dimensional work must be ready to hang without sawtooth hangers, and pieces must fit through a standard door. The four jurors are all working artists: ceramicist Alexis Moyer, mixed-media abstractionist Chris Hagie, painter Gwen Lowery, and Karin Denson, whose glitch-based paintings, photomontages and collages sit between nature and technology. Jury results 7 September, work due by 25 September, exhibition 1 October – 2 November 2026 with an opening reception on 2 October. The gallery takes 40% commission. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: $35 + $5 each additional work. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Circuito OFF 2026 · NARNIMMAGINARIA
item.description: The free and independent section of NARNIMMAGINARIA, the photography festival staged in the historic centre of Narni, Umbria, and run by the Associazione culturale SATOR. Now in its 11th edition, the 2026 theme is "Through human landscapes": the traces people leave in the places they inhabit and reshape, and the invisible territories of their stories and emotions. Documentary, narrative, conceptual, artistic and experimental readings are all admitted, and entry is open to photographers of any age, nationality or background. Three categories: Single Shot, a single photograph, with fine-art printing and installation handled entirely by the organisers; Triptych, three photographs or a single panel supplied already printed and hung in the bars, restaurants, shops and other businesses of the centre rather than in galleries, with installation optionally delegated to the organisers for €35; and Stories, a printed sequence of 8 to 18 images at 30×40 cm, framed by the organisers. Entrants can apply to one, two or all three categories and submit more than one work in each, paying a €15 contribution per category. Everything goes by email as a single ZIP folder. The exhibition runs 17 October to 2 November 2026; printed works are due 8 October. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: €15 per category. Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: ROOTS · Fototeka
item.description: Second open call from Fototeka, a Romanian analog photography hub and publisher, for a new collective printed volume following its first book Sequence 01, which brought together 93 photographers. The theme is ROOTS — origin, belonging, memory and connection, read literally or metaphorically: natural elements, portraits, archives, rituals, personal and collective histories. Roots usually remain hidden, yet they shape what becomes visible. Only film-based photography is eligible; digital and AI-generated images are excluded. Up to ten analog photographs per submission, minimum 3000 pixels on the long side. The 50 RON (about €10) fee supports the editorial, design, printing and presentation work and does not guarantee inclusion: the curatorial team sequences the book, so a submission may end up represented by no photographs, one, or several. Selected work may also be featured on Fototeka's online platforms. The album is planned for October–November 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: 50 RON (~€10). Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Under Many Moons: Asian and Pacific Islander Art, Identity, and Community · Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description: Juried exhibition at Sebastopol Center for the Arts presented with AAPIC North Bay and the Many Moons Festival, the annual autumn gathering in Sebastopol that uplifts Asian American and Pacific Islander culture, creativity and community. The show explores identity, heritage, belonging and cultural expression. While it centres AAPI voices and perspectives, artists of all backgrounds engaging thoughtfully with the themes are invited to submit work reflecting personal and collective narratives shaped by culture, place and lived experience. All media, photography included. Entry is $35 for one application of up to three images, with $10 for each additional application. Work must fit through a 7' by 7' gallery door and on an 8-foot wall; the centre's installation team can hang selected pieces. Juror Patricia Wakida is a community historian, linoleum block carver and letterpress printer who apprenticed as a papermaker in Gifu, Japan. Work must have been made in the last five years and not shown at SebArts before. Notifications 14 August; exhibition runs 26 September – 11 October 2026 with an opening reception on 26 September. — Deadline: August 4, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: CCAN 2026 — 10th Annual National Juried Art Competition · Center for Contemporary Arts
item.description: Tenth edition of the Center for Contemporary Arts' national juried competition in downtown Abilene, Texas. Over $7,000 is awarded annually across 11 media categories — including a dedicated 2D Photography (Film & Digital) category, each with a $500 first prize — plus a $750 juror's award and a $1,000 best of show. Juror Carlyn Ray is a Dallas-based glass artist known for large-scale installations. Open to artists 18 and over; work must be original, made within the last three years, and the image submitted must be the piece delivered. Wall-mounted 2D work is capped at 48 inches framed on its longest dimension, wall-mounted 3D at 36 by 36 inches and freestanding 3D at 36 inches in any dimension, with a 50 lb weight limit. No video or mural work. Entry is $35 for one image and $20 for each additional, limit three. Notifications 1 September; exhibition runs 10 October – 21 November 2026, with the opening reception and awards on 10 October. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: $35 for 1 image, $20 each additional. Prize: $7,000 in cash awards.

item.title: Contemporary Figures: A National Juried Exhibition · LHUCA
item.description: National juried exhibition of contemporary figurative work at LHUCA, the Louise Hopkins Underwood Center for the Arts in Lubbock, Texas. The call asks how the body is understood in relation to environment, society and technology: scientific advances have made us more aware of the composition and processes of the human body while blurring the boundaries between the human and the nonhuman, and the body remains intimately tied to identity and to how we move in space and in relation to others. Figurative work addressing a range of themes and presenting the body in unique ways is welcome. Open to painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, collage, photography, digital art, ceramics, books and textiles; all works must hang on the wall and are capped at 36 by 36 inches, with plexiglass glazing required on anything shipped. Open to artists 18 or over living in the United States. Entry is $25 for up to two images. Cash prizes of $300, $200 and $100 plus a $50 honorable mention. Notifications 11 September 2026; the exhibition runs 2 October – 28 November 2026, with opening receptions on 2 October and 6 November during the First Friday Art Trail, which draws an estimated 5,000 visitors a month to LHUCA's galleries. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $300 / $200 / $100.

item.title: Call for Proposals 2027 · LHUCA
item.description: LHUCA invites exhibition proposals for its 2027–2028 gallery season in Lubbock, Texas. Four galleries are available and each exhibition runs two consecutive months. All visual art media are accepted, including photography. Free to apply: submit a PDF with 5–10 digital images, an artist statement of up to 500 words, contact details and preferred dates. An artist stipend is available for travelling artists, and work can be for sale or not. Proposals are encouraged but not required to respond to the character of a particular gallery; floor plans are published alongside the call. Artists who have exhibited with LHUCA before can only reapply every five years. The galleries draw an estimated 5,000-plus visitors a month during the First Friday Art Trail. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Chaos: An Exploration of Disorder, Meaning, and Possibility · Bitfactory Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at Bitfactory Gallery & Studios in Denver seeking two-dimensional, wall-hanging work that responds to chaos — visible or invisible, personal or collective, destructive or generative. It may appear as a fractured system, an unsettled world, a difficult relationship, a crowded mind, or the moment when certainty gives way; it may be imposed on us, created by us, or necessary before change can occur. Literal, emotional, psychological, social, symbolic and abstract approaches are all welcome. All 2D mediums qualify, including photography, painting, collage, fiber and textile, pastel, graphite and print works. Open to Colorado residents aged 18 and over; 3–10 images, $25 entry with $5 per additional image. Juror W. Max Thomason. Notifications 10 August; exhibition runs 21 August – 12 September 2026 with an opening reception on 21 August, 6–9pm. — Deadline: August 9, 2026. Fee: $25 for 3 images, $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Juried Exhibition · Rawls Museum Arts
item.description: Annual all-media juried exhibition at Rawls Museum Arts, a non-profit museum founded in 1958 in Courtland, Virginia, dedicated to making the arts accessible through exhibitions, education and community outreach. $1,000 in total prize money: $500 first place, $300 second and $200 third. Artists of all ages are encouraged to apply. Work must be original and created without the aid of an instructor or kit; AI-generated work, or work derived in whole or part from AI, is not eligible. Entry is $35 for up to three submissions, one image per artwork. Pieces cannot exceed 50 pounds or 45 inches in the longest dimension, and all selected work must be hand-delivered — no shipping — by 2pm on 12 September 2026. Co-curated by museum staff with juror Allen TenBusschen, a contemporary realist painter who chairs the art department at the University of Lynchburg. Notifications by 15 August; exhibition runs 19 September – 23 October 2026, and the museum takes a 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35 for 3 works. Prize: $500 / $300 / $200.

item.title: Common Ground in the Heartland: Reflecting on America at 250 · Washington Pavilion Visual Arts Center
item.description: Free-to-enter juried exhibition at the Visual Arts Center of the Washington Pavilion in Sioux Falls, marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. The centre invites artists from across the Midwest to reflect on the people, places and experiences that shape a shared story — from small towns and family farms to growing cities and tribal communities — in a region long a crossroads of cultures, traditions, industries and ideas. The exhibition explores the values, traditions and relationships that bring people together while recognising the diverse experiences that define communities, with suggested themes including community and belonging, cultural heritage, land and stewardship. All mediums are welcome, photography included, and up to five images may be submitted. Artists from the Midwest or with a connection to the region are encouraged to apply, though entry is not formally restricted, and artists at every career stage are invited. Work must not exceed 60 inches or 50 lbs and arrives ready to install; the centre insures it and splits sales 70/30 in the artist's favour. Notifications 5 August, with work due 20 August — the show then runs an unusually long 28 August 2026 – 21 February 2027. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: REBUILDING: Art as Renewal, Possibility, and Purpose · Art League Rhode Island
item.description: Juried exhibition at the Art League Rhode Island Gallery and Tiernan Hallway Gallery in Pawtucket, asking how art can restore what has been fractured — making whole what has been broken, empowering what has been silenced and reclaiming what connects us. The theme is not about loss but about what gets built next: how art can reassemble meaning, mend relationships and model balance in a world seeking repair. Open to any artist 18 or over, in all 2D and 3D media; 1–5 images plus an optional video, $35 entry with $10 per additional media file. Work must be original and previously unexhibited with ALRI, and anything conceived or created with generative AI is ineligible. Jurors are Kerry Phillips, a Miami-based installation artist working with found objects and site-responsive materials, and Meaghan Kent, independent curator, founder of the nonprofit Site95 and former Deputy Director at MOCA North Miami. Awards are $500 first, $300 second and $150 third, plus two honorable mentions and a People's Choice. Notification by 4 November; exhibition runs 5 December 2026 – 17 January 2027. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–5 images), $10 each additional. Prize: $500 / $300 / $150.

item.title: Fresh Squeezed 2026 Annual Juried Show · Suffolk Art League
item.description: The Suffolk Art League's annual juried exhibition at the Suffolk Art Gallery in Suffolk, Virginia, marking the league's 50th anniversary and asking for artists' latest, never-before-seen work. Open to artists over 18 in all mediums: the gallery's own listing rules out only video and audio, though the CaFÉ entry also excludes digital, so anyone printing digitally is worth checking with first. Work must not have been previously exhibited at the gallery and must have been completed within the last two years. Members submit up to three works for $30; non-members pay $55 and full-time student non-members $50, both of which include an individual membership. First place is $500 plus the opportunity to present a one-person show at the Suffolk Art Gallery in 2027, with $300 second and $200 third. 2D work must be framed, wired or gallery-wrapped — no sawtooth hangers — and 3D work is displayed on pedestals provided by the gallery. Notifications by 25 September; exhibition runs 24 October – 4 December 2026. The league retains a 30% consignment on works sold. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: $30 members, $55 non-members, +$5 each extra. Prize: $500 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Backwards/Forwards · Light Art Space
item.description: Juried exhibition of handmade prints at Light Art Space in Silver City, New Mexico, staged as the juried show of the Southwest Print Fiesta. The brief asks artists to treat time as material — memory, pressure, inheritance, repetition, rupture and possibility — looking backward at the histories that shape us and forward at futures we imagine or fear. All work must be handmade prints made by the artist in the last five years using traditional printmaking and/or photographic processes: silver gelatin, photopolymer and copperplate gravure, cyanotype, vandyke, gum bichromate, palladium, platinum, carbon, salt, chemigram, lumen, argyrotype, oil print, chlorophyll, instant transfers and lifts, alongside etching, woodcut, lithography, screenprint and letterpress. 3D and experimental work encouraged. Digital processes are allowed only where meaningfully integrated with handmade methods; AI-generated and purely digital prints are ineligible. Juror Terran J. Last Gun, Piikani artist based in Santa Fe and an Art in America 2026 New Talent. Open worldwide to artists 18 and over. $35 for three works, $10 per additional piece up to ten, $20 for full-time students. Work must arrive ready to hang but framing is not required. Exhibition runs 8 October – 7 November 2026 with a reception and juror talk on 9 October; gallery takes 50% on sales and artists cover shipping both ways. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $35 for 3 works. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: PhEST Portfolio Reviews 2026
item.description: Free portfolio reviews at PhEST – See Beyond the Sea, the international photography and contemporary art festival in Monopoli, Puglia. Reviews run 8 August (3–6pm) and 9 August (10am–1pm) at the Saint Leonardo Monastery, in 20-minute one-to-one sessions; each photographer can book up to three reviews, one per reviewer. Completed projects and work in progress are both welcome, presented as prints or on a device. The 2026 reviewers are Josh Lustig, picture editor at FT Weekend Magazine; Erik Vroons, writer and editor at Over Magazine; Veronica Daltri, photo editor at Il Manifesto; Krzysztof Candrowicz, curator and co-founder of Łódź Fotofestiwal; artist and curator Francesca Seravalle; and Hannah Watson, director of Trolley Books. Sessions with Lustig, Vroons, Candrowicz and Watson are held in English only. Registration is free and online until 2 August, with limited on-site places from 10 minutes before each session. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Photobook Open Call ZUM/IMS 2026
item.description: Annual photobook call from ZUM magazine, the contemporary art department and the Photography Library of the Instituto Moreira Salles in São Paulo, running since 2017 to deepen the institute’s links with contemporary photography publishing. Open to publications released from October 2025 onwards, from any country, from publishers of any size or self-published — dummies and prototypes are not accepted. Entry is free and open to any nationality. Selected publications each receive R$300 towards costs, are presented during Festival ZUM in November 2026 and stay on display in the IMS Photography Library; a panel of external guests and IMS staff then awards the three best publications R$2,000 each. Enter through the online form and post or hand-deliver a copy to IMS Paulista — books must arrive by 26 September 2026. All submitted publications are accessioned into the IMS Photography Library and catalogued for public consultation unless the author asks for the copy back within 30 days of the shortlist. — Deadline: September 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: R$2,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Duets: A Collab Show · Avondale Arts Alliance
item.description: Collaboration-only show at the Avondale Arts Center, the volunteer-run gallery of the Avondale Arts Alliance just east of Atlanta. Every work in the September–October exhibition must be made by exactly two artists together; entrants can submit up to six pieces and may pair with a different collaborator on each one. Work that does not meet the two-artist rule is disqualified. Only one of the two collaborators submits the entry. Entry is $15 for up to three pieces and $30 for up to six, paid by Square link; artists 18 and under enter free with a voucher code, and the alliance asks anyone facing financial hardship to get in touch. Open to Atlanta and surrounding artists, and work must be hand delivered on 5–6 September — no shipping. Status emails by 29 August; exhibition runs 12 September – 24 October 2026 with a closing reception. All work must be for sale and the alliance retains 30%. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: $15 for 3 works, $30 for 6. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Wild & Domestic 2026 · Medford Arts Center
item.description: All-media juried exhibition about animals — wild and domestic — at the Medford Arts Center, a 501(c)(3) community arts centre on North Main Street in Medford, New Jersey, funded in part by the New Jersey State Council on the Arts. Juror of awards is Terri Amig; chairs are Diane Emerson and Susan Barnes. Open to artists 18 and over, up to three original pieces each, none previously shown at MAC. Entry is $20/$30/$40 for members and $30/$40/$50 for non-members for one, two or three works. The show runs online and in the gallery from 7 August to 3 September 2026, with in-gallery display limited to accepted work that can be hand delivered; awards reception 7 August. Cash awards for first, second and third place plus three honourable mentions. All work must be for sale and the centre takes 30% commission. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: $30 for 1 work ($20 members). Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Trinity Art Show 10th Annual — Living Water
item.description: Tenth annual national juried exhibition at the Lexis Gallery, Trinity Cathedral in Sacramento, a progressive Episcopal community that runs the show as an open conversation about faith rather than a devotional display. The 2026 theme is 'Living Water' — work that explicitly references faith and work simply in conversation with the spirituality the theme suggests are equally welcome. All media including photography; juried by Ryan M. Reynolds, Chair of Art and Art History at Santa Clara University. $5,000 in cash awards: $3,000 first place, $1,500 second, $500 honorable mention. Open to US artists with original work made in the last five years and not exhibited in Sacramento within the last two. Exhibition runs 3 October – 8 November 2026 with an opening reception on 3 October. — Deadline: August 19, 2026. Fee: $45 for 3 works + $5 each additional. Prize: $5,000 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Confluence of Art Annual 2026 · Pablo Center at the Confluence
item.description: Free-to-enter juried annual at the James Hansen Gallery inside Pablo Center at the Confluence, the arts centre where the Chippewa and Eau Claire rivers meet in western Wisconsin. Around 50 pieces are selected across 2D, 3D and multimedia from artists in the Chippewa Valley, the Midwest and beyond, and a judge picks four of them for cash prizes announced at the October awards reception. Up to three pieces per artist, original and made in the last five years, not previously shown at Pablo Center within two years. Submissions go by email with a bio or statement, title, size, medium and price. Work is dropped off 1–8 September; the exhibition runs 28 September – 22 November 2026, awards reception 9 October. Gallery commission is 40%, or 30% for Pablo Center members. — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Cash prizes + Exhibition.

item.title: 14th Annual Eastern West Virginia Juried Exhibition · Berkeley Arts Council
item.description: Annual open-theme juried exhibition at Berkeley Art Works, the Berkeley Arts Council's gallery in downtown Martinsburg. Open to artists 18 and over living in Berkeley, Grant, Hampshire, Hardy, Jefferson, Mineral, Morgan or Pendleton County — a deliberately regional show for the eastern panhandle and highlands of West Virginia. Original two- or three-dimensional work in any medium or technique, abstract, representational or non-representational, completed in the last three years and not previously exhibited at Berkeley Art Works. Juried by Sonya Evanisko, Professor of Art and Painting/Drawing Coordinator at Shepherd University, who selects a Best in Show, a Merit Award and an Honorable Mention. On view 24 September – 15 November 2026. — Deadline: August 27, 2026. Fee: $40 for 2 works + $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Figuratively Speaking · Wallkill River Center for the Arts
item.description: Regional exhibition on the human figure at the Wallkill River Center for the Arts in Montgomery, in New York's Hudson Valley. The call asks how we see ourselves and how we see others: 'With all the special attributes that make each of us an individual, the one truth that we can't get around is that we all share humanity, for better or worse. Tell us a story.' Juried by painter John McGiff (BFA SUNY Purchase, MFA University of Pennsylvania, two Delaware Division of the Arts painting fellowships). One entry of up to four pieces per artist, $25, waived for WRCA artist members. Open to US residents 18 and over; work must be hand delivered by 8 November — no shipping. AI-generated work and reproductions such as giclée prints of paintings are not accepted. 2D works up to 30 inches wide by 40 inches high including the frame, priced by the artist between $200 and $9,000. Gallery takes 30% commission; exhibition runs 14 November – 20 December 2026. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The In Between · Ninety-Seven Modern
item.description: Detroit-rooted online gallery Ninety-Seven Modern invites emerging artists to submit black-and-white work exploring the transient nature of the in between — the dual realities most of us live in at any given moment: recollection and the present, anger and love, stagnation and momentum. Black and white is framed as a reminder that both can exist together, with or without a fight for dominance. All mediums are welcome. Entry is a flat $5 for up to three works, submitted by email with a third-person bio; the gallery does not accept AI-generated imagery. Ninety-Seven Modern also lists selected artists' original works for sale through its shop. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Quiet Image II · The Ace Project
item.description: Second edition of The Quiet Image at The Ace Project, a contemporary photography space on Zaagmolendrift in Rotterdam. The call asks photographers based in the Netherlands and Belgium for work exploring the relationship between nature and the human body. Up to five works may be submitted by email for review; submission is free. Selected photographers are invited for a personal conversation at the gallery, and their work must be professionally printed and framed at their own cost — participation also carries a contribution fee towards exhibition costs, which the gallery does not publish in advance. The exhibition runs 25 September to 18 October 2026. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free (contribution fee if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Amazing Abstracts 2026 · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, for artists who have declared their independence from portraying reality — abstract work built on line, shape, colour, form and gestural mark, from drip paintings and colour fields to geometric designs and abstract patterns found in nature, architecture and human activity. Photography and photo-based work are accepted alongside painting, printmaking, mixed media, drawing and sculpture. Open to US residents 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award with a special exhibit in the gallery's second exhibition room, an honorable mention carrying free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from all artists shown during the year. The gallery takes 30% commission on sales and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs December 19, 2026 – January 16, 2027. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Variations of Yellow 2026 · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, built around a single colour. Yellow carries warmth, joy, spontaneity and optimism — and, in its other register, cowardice and deceit; the gallery asks how the colour works in your practice, whether it floods the frame or appears in a single object, whether it is decorative or structural. Realistic or imaginary, representational or abstract, all interpretations are welcome. Photography and photo collage are accepted alongside painting, printmaking, mixed media, drawing and sculpture. Open to US residents 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award with a special exhibit in the gallery's second exhibition room, an honorable mention carrying free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity. Exhibition runs December 19, 2026 – January 16, 2027. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Changing Seasons · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on seasonal change as a transformative force. The gallery invites three layers of response: nature (landscapes and seascapes through the year, the rhythms of growth, transition and decay), human activity (swimming, skiing, picnicking, gardening — or figures struggling against weather and terrain), and emotional effect (spring as renewal, summer as freedom, autumn as melancholy, winter as isolation). Photography and photo-based work are accepted alongside painting, printmaking, mixed media, drawing and sculpture. Open to US residents 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award with a special exhibit in the gallery's second exhibition room, an honorable mention carrying free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity. Exhibition runs December 19, 2026 – January 16, 2027. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Unbound 2: Anything Goes · Studio ACE
item.description: Second edition of ACE Gallery's open-themed juried exhibition in Oceanside, California, returning after an enthusiastic response to the inaugural show. The gallery asks artists to release expectations, defy their own rules and submit the work that excites them most — Unbound honours process over perfection and passion over polish, welcoming confident statements, quiet reflections and unexpected juxtapositions alike. Photography sits alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media and fully experimental work. Studio ACE is an arts-education nonprofit founded in 2016 that runs free art programmes for neurodivergent children, teens and adults; ACE Gallery, its exhibition space, opened in early 2024 and shows both emerging and established artists. Submit 3 to 20 works. Accepted work is notified August 21, with drop-off September 11–12. Exhibition runs September 19 – October 22, 2026, with an opening reception on September 19. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $25 (3 works) + $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art Comes Alive 2026 · ADC Fine Art
item.description: Seventeenth edition of ADC Fine Art's annual exhibition and awards gala, held in the gallery's 13,000 sq ft space in Cincinnati's Over-the-Rhine and long nicknamed the 'Academy Awards for Artists'. Around 250 living artists are shown across all mediums, photography included. What distinguishes it from a typical juried show is the award structure: ADC puts the total at over $450,000, though most of that is its own services valued in-house rather than cash — ten gallery representation contracts valued at $8,500 each, two solo shows, six group shows, print and digital magazine features and SmartSell memberships, alongside $74,100 in juror awards and $175,000 in purchase awards. The jury is drawn from ADC's own staff — president Litsa Spanos, gallery director Annie Kautz, marketing director Amy Scalia and assistant gallery director Chance Smith — with more jurors to be announced. Entry is $25 per work, with the last entry free on applications of four or more. Results are announced October 2, work arrives at the gallery by October 16, and the opening night and awards ceremony fall on November 7. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $25 per work. Prize: $175,000 purchase awards + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Changing Asia 2026 · China Daily Asia Pacific
item.description: The Changing Asia photo exhibition, organised by China Daily with the Asia News Network, returns with the theme "Moments of Connection: Smiles and Hands of the Asia-Pacific" — a phrase drawn from the 2026 APEC leaders' meeting slogan, and a brief that asks for real interactions: collaboration, trade, mutual assistance, cultural exchange. Within that frame the call keeps its long-standing threads — the social, economic, environmental and cultural shifts reshaping the continent, stories of resilience told through individual communities, and Asia's diversity documented in its contrasts as much as its connections. Entry is free and open to photographers worldwide; work must have been made since 1 January 2023, and basic colour correction and filters are accepted. Selected images are shown in the exhibition, published in the accompanying photo book and awarded a certificate. Earlier editions launched in Bangkok (2022) and Jakarta (2023) before moving online in 2024, which drew over 1,400 submissions from more than 40 countries. The 2026 exhibition opens on 26 October at the Shenzhen Research Institute of The Chinese University of Hong Kong, ahead of the APEC meeting. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Photo book.

item.title: Fire · A Photographer's Place
item.description: Fire as an elemental force but also as an idea. The gallery invites photographic work that engages with fire as metaphor, condition and experience rather than simply as subject matter — images that consider the elemental through the psychological, the social, the environmental or the poetic. Work that reveals fire through gesture, light, atmosphere, colour, landscape, portraiture, abstraction or narrative is welcome, where the photograph evokes rather than describes. Not every fire burns. Open to photographers of all levels, in colour or black and white. Selected work hangs in Gallery X at the front of the space in Raleigh from September 4 to 30, 2026, with an opening reception on September 4, and is then presented on the gallery website year-round. Accepted artists may optionally have their work printed in-house on the gallery's Canon imagePROGRAF Pro-1100. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 5 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Monochrome · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group exhibition of monochromatic photography — not limited to black and white but including sepia, cyan and other single-colour tonal ranges, where the absence of a colour range carries meaning as a deliberate artistic choice rather than a technical necessity. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD; founder/director of PH21 Gallery, Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian). One Curator's Choice winner receives three complimentary entries to future PH21 themed calls, and up to three honourable mentions are announced. Reduced rates of €15 (early bird) or €20 apply for students, unwaged applicants and those from low-income economies. Early bird deadline September 7, final deadline September 14. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, November 14 – December 8, 2026. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Guildford Festival of the Arts 2026
item.description: Open call for the 2026 edition of this Surrey arts festival, accepting any visual art of any medium that can be displayed in a gallery or on a screen — photography included. There is no set theme. Two tracks run in parallel: an Open Call for artists aged 18 and over, and a separate Student Open Call. The 2026 judging panel is Sally Varah MBE DL, Councillor Jane Tyson (Mayor of Guildford), artist Monica Popham and photographer Andy Newbold. Everyone's first submission is free; further artworks go through a separate paid form. Alongside the £1,000 first prize there is a £500 runner-up prize, a £150 gift voucher for the student winner and an exhibition at New House Art Space for the Public Vote winner. Selected artists are notified by email in late August or early September and may sell work through the festival team during the festival, on which a 15% commission is retained to fund the following year's edition. Artists should submit once; a series, diptych or triptych should be sent as a single image encompassing the whole piece. The inaugural 2025 festival drew over 2,400 visits across 20 venues. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Pretty Ugly — Student Photography Competition 2026/27 · ILFORD Photo
item.description: A darkroom print competition asking students to explore the idea that ugliness is often just a matter of perspective. A rough texture, an unusual face, a forgotten space — under the right conditions the overlooked becomes extraordinary, and perceived imperfections such as scars, wear and age can tell powerful stories of resilience and character. Entrants are challenged to question first impressions and capture their own interpretation of 'pretty ugly'. All images must be shot on ILFORD or Kentmere black and white film and hand-printed by the student in the darkroom on ILFORD or Kentmere black and white papers; digital submissions are not accepted and prints must be posted with an entry label firmly attached to the back of each. Minimum print size is 8x10 inches, and images that have won other competitions or been published by a third party are not eligible. Multiple entries are encouraged, and lecturers may bundle a class's prints in one package. Open to students of any age anywhere in the world taking a full or part-time course at a school, college or university; prints go to HARMAN technology in Mobberley, Cheshire, or to its Seattle address. ILFORD points students without darkroom access to its Pop-Up Darkrooms and community darkroom locator. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: £200 in ILFORD products + 35mm film camera.

item.title: Let Our Hearts Speak · Rethinking Eastern Europe
item.description: Open call for a collective publication from Rethinking Eastern Europe, an artist collective founded in 2024 by Polish visual artist Zula Rabikowska that now gathers around 50 artists from Central and Eastern Europe, the Balkans and the diaspora. Taking its title from bell hooks — 'when we love we can let our hearts speak' — the call invites work that engages with 'Eastern Europe' as a lived, shifting and often contested space: not only geography, but memory, inheritance, migration and emotional landscape. The publication brings together visual and written works reflecting on intimacy, love, identity, displacement and belonging, and understands the region as plural and expansive, shaped by diasporas, post-socialist realities and personal archives. Open to artists of any age, nationality, location and career stage, including those working outside institutions. Published in collective print and digital formats with careful artist attribution; fee waivers are available on request. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: £8 (waivers available). Prize: £150 + Publication.

item.title: James Balog Earth Vision Awards · Denver Art Museum
item.description: Juried prizes supporting photographers responding to today's complex environmental issues, organised and produced by the Denver Art Museum with funds endowed by James Balog and other donors, and awarded every two years. The awards recognise sustained commitment and significant accomplishment in photography that bears witness to the relationship between humans and the environment and challenges people to build healthier, more sustainable relationships with nature. A three-member jury of expert photo professionals reviews all entries and may contact entrants for clarification before final decisions; fabricated photographs, cloning, excessive colour manipulation and AI-generated content are not considered. First prize is $40,000 ($30,000 on award, $10,000 twelve to eighteen months later) and the finalist receives $25,000 ($19,000 on award, $6,000 later). Applicants submit a portfolio of 10 to 20 photographs — falling outside that range is grounds for disqualification — with an artist statement describing firsthand experience and the environmental significance of the work, an explanation of the intended project and its anticipated impact, and a resume or exhibition history. Open to photographers worldwide aged 21 or over; previous winners and finalists are not eligible. The call opens September 1, 2026, winners are announced in January 2027, and awards are presented at the Denver Art Museum in March 2027. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $40,000.

item.title: Women United ART PRIZE 2026 — Photography & Printmaking · Women United Art Movement
item.description: Annual international prize for women-identifying artists, with a dedicated Photography & Printmaking category covering all types of photography and printmaking including cyanotype. First place in each category receives USD 500 cash, an in-depth interview in Women United Art Magazine Special Edition 2026, a podcast interview, a virtual solo exhibition with 3D gallery tour, an artist directory profile, a USD 250 printing gift card, and free entries to 2027 opportunities. Second and third place receive interviews, an online group exhibit and virtual 3D tour. Places 4–10 are featured in the magazine and group exhibit. Regular entries close 31 August; a last-minute phase runs 1–15 September at higher fees. Fee waivers available for artists in countries affected by war, natural disaster, or the suppression of women’s rights. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: €16–€45. Prize: $500 + Publication + Exhibition.

item.title: Around, Above, Below · Van Der Plas Gallery
item.description: Group exhibition at Van Der Plas Gallery on Manhattan’s Lower East Side exploring perception and the experience of daily life as we move through urban environments, rural landscapes and the spaces in between. The show sets up a dialogue between the built environment and the natural world, asking artists to explore the balance between tension and harmony. Artists working in all media are encouraged to submit, including photography. On view 1–15 October 2026 with an opening reception on 1 October, 6–8pm. Submissions form part of the gallery’s year-round Open Call Program and remain in consideration for future exhibitions beyond this cycle. — Deadline: September 17, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Maledetto Cane — Next Photobook Open Call
item.description: Rome-based independent photobook publisher autoproduzioni Maledetto Cane is looking for a photographic body of work with a coherent authorial visual language and the potential to be published as a monographic photobook. The selected body of work will be developed into a monograph by the press. All submissions are also considered for inclusion in Maledetto Cane #3, the third issue of the collective periodical. Submit a portfolio of no fewer than 40 JPEGs by email or WeTransfer, with a short synopsis or artist statement; a draft PDF of the proposed book may be included but is not required. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Photobook publication.

item.title: The Book Project: Landscape 2026 · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Juried call for a published hardbound photography book on landscape photography, part of Black Box Gallery’s Book Project series of focused hardbound books each built around a single theme. From grand landscapes to intimate details, the gallery is looking for work that demonstrates the photographer’s own connection to nature. Ten photographers will be selected with five photographs each. The 12 × 12 inch hardbound book is printed by Blurb and sold through the Black Box Gallery website. All rights to the photographs remain with the photographer and files are used only for the book printing. Photographers are notified 7–10 days after the deadline. Apply by paying the entry fee via PayPal and emailing your entry. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: Emerging Berlin · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: Year-round local open call from Fotografiska’s Emerging programme, dedicated to supporting and showcasing image-makers with a distinctive visual language whose photographic practice embodies, represents and shapes a part of Berlin. Selected artists are given a platform at Fotografiska Berlin through solo or group exhibitions. An emerging artist here means a photographer or image-maker whose work has not yet been presented in an institutional museum exhibition but who has already developed a recognisable visual language — the definition is not tied to age, years of experience or formal education, and includes self-taught artists and those working outside traditional pathways. The call has run on an ongoing basis since 12 March 2026; submissions are reviewed by the jury every six months, followed by a curation period of up to two weeks. Open to anyone 18 or over — the Berlin connection is a criterion for the work, not a residency requirement. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Emerging Stockholm · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: Year-round local open call from Fotografiska’s Emerging programme, running since 2023 and dedicated to supporting and showcasing early-career image-makers from across Sweden. Roughly three artists a year are invited to present their work within Fotografiska Stockholm’s exhibition programme, alongside opportunities for professional dialogue and development. Material is reviewed on an ongoing basis throughout the year, and only artists whose work moves forward in the internal review are contacted. Applicants must be 18 or over and based in Sweden. An emerging artist here means a photographer or image-maker whose work has not yet been presented in an institutional museum exhibition but who has already developed a recognisable visual language — not tied to age, years of experience or formal education, and including self-taught artists. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Fotografiska Stockholm exhibition.

item.title: Quinn Emanuel Silicon Valley Artist-in-Residence 2026
item.description: Four-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel's Silicon Valley office in Redwood Shores for emerging and mid-career artists working in any medium, including photography. Two artists are selected per cycle and each receives $5,000 per month for four months ($20,000 total) plus a materials allowance of up to $1,500. The residency begins November 2026; a one-month exhibition follows, mounted with curator Alexis Hyde in a venue agreed with the artists, and work may be offered for sale. The studio is an office inside the Silicon Valley location, in a 24/7 keycard-access building with parking if needed. Open only to artists living in the greater Bay Area, as regular in-person studio use is expected; international artists may apply but must secure their own visas. Preference goes to underrepresented artists in the early or middle stages of their career. No education requirement, and the firm will make accommodations for disabled artists. Apply by email with a 500-word proposal, a CV and an 8–10 image portfolio as a single PDF under 20MB. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $20,000 stipend + $1,500 materials + Exhibition.

item.title: Opulent Mobility 2026
item.description: Opulent Mobility is an international annual exhibit that asks artists to re-imagine disability as opulent and powerful rather than merely functional. The 2026 focus is disabled joy — as the call puts it, at a time when rights are being dismantled and images erased, deliberate acts of joy are powerful and essential. Curated by founder A. Laura Brody with disability arts activist and photographer Anthony Tusler, and supported by the Numotion Foundation. Two-dimensional and sculptural work, music files and performances on digital media are all accepted; photographers may submit digital files rather than shipping prints, which makes the show genuinely open to international entrants. A flat $20 fee covers gallery rental and insurance for up to ten works, and is waived on request if it causes hardship. The exhibit runs December 6–20, 2026 in person in Los Angeles and online; the gallery takes 30% of any sale. Accessibility is built in: artwork descriptions in text and audio, and ASL interpreters at the opening and the online artist talk. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $20 (up to 10 works), waived on request. Prize: Exhibition.
